properties.title: Bertha Benz's long-distance drive
properties.why_famous: The first long-distance automobile journey demonstrated that the motorcar could be practical transport.
properties.route_summary: Mannheim to Pforzheim via Heidelberg, Wiesloch and Bruchsal; a different return through Bretten.
properties.source_title: Mercedes-Benz: Bertha Benz and the long-distance journey
properties.geometry_note: Town-level outward and return reconstruction. Connecting lines do not claim the exact unpaved road alignment of 1888.
properties.description: Town-level outward and return reconstruction. Connecting lines do not claim the exact unpaved road alignment of 1888.
properties.overview: The first long-distance automobile journey demonstrated that the motorcar could be practical transport.

properties.title: First U.S. cross-country automobile drive
properties.why_famous: Jackson, Crocker and their dog Bud completed the first automobile crossing of the United States.
properties.route_summary: San Francisco to New York through the northern Rockies and Midwest.
properties.source_title: Smithsonian: Crossing the Country
properties.geometry_note: Chronological stop corridor, not a trace of individual roads or detours; no transcontinental highway existed.
properties.description: Chronological stop corridor, not a trace of individual roads or detours; no transcontinental highway existed.
properties.overview: Jackson, Crocker and their dog Bud completed the first automobile crossing of the United States.

properties.title: Peking–Paris Motor Race
properties.why_famous: Borghese's Itala crossed Asia and Europe, proving that automobiles could survive an unprecedented continental journey.
properties.route_summary: Beijing through Mongolia and Siberia to European Russia, Germany and Paris.
properties.source_title: Louwman Museum: The Peking–Paris Automobile Race in 1907
properties.geometry_note: Borghese-focused named-place corridor; Gobi tracks and period roads are not surveyed geometry.
properties.description: Borghese-focused named-place corridor; Gobi tracks and period roads are not surveyed geometry.
properties.overview: Borghese's Itala crossed Asia and Europe, proving that automobiles could survive an unprecedented continental journey.

properties.title: New York–Paris Race
properties.why_famous: Schuster's Thomas Flyer won the intercontinental endurance contest through North America, Asia and Europe.
properties.route_summary: New York to San Francisco by road, sea transfer to Valdez and back to Seattle, then via Japan to Vladivostok by ship; across Eurasia by road to Paris.
properties.source_title: The Henry Ford: 1908 New York to Paris Race
properties.geometry_note: Separate road and ship corridors. The American team landed in Alaska but did not drive across the Bering Strait; the Siberian roads remain generalized.
properties.description: Separate road and ship corridors. The American team landed in Alaska but did not drive across the Bering Strait; the Siberian roads remain generalized.
properties.overview: Schuster's Thomas Flyer won the intercontinental endurance contest through North America, Asia and Europe.

properties.source_title: Smithsonian: Crossing the Country

properties.description: Named-city reconstruction; individual farm roads, bridges and detours remain unverified.

properties.title: London–Brighton Emancipation Run
properties.why_famous: The celebratory motor run marked the relaxation of Britain's restrictive motoring rules.
properties.route_summary: London to Brighton through Surrey and Sussex, including Reigate and Crawley corridors.
properties.source_title: Motor Car Club's original 1896 route instructions (Royal Automobile Club archive)
properties.geometry_note: The original 1896 instructions name Croydon, Reigate, Crawley and other intermediate places. These anchors follow that itinerary; individual road curves and vehicle positions remain approximate.

properties.overview: The celebratory motor run marked the relaxation of Britain's restrictive motoring rules.

properties.source_title: Pierre Giffard's account of the 1894 Paris–Rouen contest (1907)

properties.description: The event organizer's published course identifies the mapped towns in order. City points approximate the historic road corridor; the individual road alignment and vehicle positions are not traced.
properties.overview: The Paris–Rouen trial is widely considered the first organized automobile contest.

properties.title: First French Grand Prix
properties.why_famous: The inaugural Grand Prix established a demanding long public-road circuit near Le Mans.
properties.route_summary: One 103-km 1906 Sarthe circuit lap, repeated six times on each of two days.
properties.source_title: Automobile Club de l'Ouest: 1906 Grand Prix route
properties.geometry_note: Period town and bend anchors describe one 1906 loop; temporary wooden bypasses at Saint-Calais and Vibraye are schematic, and repeated laps are metadata only.
properties.description: Period town and bend anchors describe one 1906 loop; temporary wooden bypasses at Saint-Calais and Vibraye are schematic, and repeated laps are metadata only.
properties.overview: The inaugural Grand Prix established a demanding long public-road circuit near Le Mans.

properties.title: First Targa Florio
properties.why_famous: The race inaugurated one of motorsport's oldest and most difficult mountain-road contests.
properties.route_summary: One Grande Circuito delle Madonie loop from Campofelice through Cerda, Petralia and Castelbuono, repeated three times.
properties.source_title: Targapedia: 1906 first Targa Florio
properties.geometry_note: The 1906 Grande circuit is represented by town anchors, not a later 72-km Piccolo loop or a claim of surveyed historic pavement.
properties.description: The 1906 Grande circuit is represented by town anchors, not a later 72-km Piccolo loop or a claim of surveyed historic pavement.
properties.overview: The race inaugurated one of motorsport's oldest and most difficult mountain-road contests.

properties.title: First Indianapolis 500
properties.why_famous: Ray Harroun won the first Indianapolis 500, one of the world's defining motor races.
properties.route_summary: One counterclockwise 1911 Indianapolis Motor Speedway oval lap, repeated 200 times.
properties.source_title: Indianapolis Motor Speedway: The first 500
properties.geometry_note: Schematic four-corner 1911 oval footprint; race distance is 200 laps, not the single rendered loop. Exact banking and track edges are not traced.
properties.description: Schematic four-corner 1911 oval footprint; race distance is 200 laps, not the single rendered loop. Exact banking and track edges are not traced.
properties.overview: Ray Harroun won the first Indianapolis 500, one of the world's defining motor races.

properties.title: Golden Flier suffrage tour
properties.why_famous: Nell Richardson and Alice Burke carried the women's suffrage campaign to towns across the United States by automobile.
properties.route_summary: New York to New Orleans, Los Angeles, San Francisco, Seattle, Minneapolis, Chicago, Detroit and back to New York.
properties.source_title: Smithsonian: Traveling for Suffrage, Part 1
properties.geometry_note: Only Smithsonian-listed principal stops are mapped, in reported order. The connectors are broad regional corridors, not the actual roads traveled.
properties.wiki_title: Women's suffrage in the United States
properties.description: Only Smithsonian-listed principal stops are mapped, in reported order. The connectors are broad regional corridors, not the actual roads traveled.
properties.overview: Nell Richardson and Alice Burke carried the women's suffrage campaign to towns across the United States by automobile.

properties.title: First Pikes Peak Auto Hill Climb
properties.why_famous: The inaugural Race to the Clouds began the famous ascent to Pikes Peak's summit.
properties.route_summary: Original Crystal Reservoir start up the Pikes Peak Highway to the summit.
properties.source_title: Pikes Peak International Hill Climb history
properties.geometry_note: 1916 starting region differs from today's route. The anchors follow named highway landmarks, with modern coordinates used only for landmark position.
properties.description: 1916 starting region differs from today's route. The anchors follow named highway landmarks, with modern coordinates used only for landmark position.
properties.overview: The inaugural Race to the Clouds began the famous ascent to Pikes Peak's summit.

properties.title: First 24 Hours of Le Mans
properties.why_famous: The inaugural 24 Hours of Le Mans began the world's best-known endurance race.
properties.route_summary: One 17.262-km 1923 Sarthe public-road circuit lap, repeated during 24 hours.
properties.source_title: Automobile Club de l'Ouest: Origin of the 24 Hours
properties.geometry_note: A 1923-specific schematic through Pontlieue, Tertre Rouge, Mulsanne, Arnage and Maison Blanche; current Le Mans barriers and chicanes are excluded.
properties.description: A 1923-specific schematic through Pontlieue, Tertre Rouge, Mulsanne, Arnage and Maison Blanche; current Le Mans barriers and chicanes are excluded.
properties.overview: The inaugural 24 Hours of Le Mans began the world's best-known endurance race.

properties.title: First Mille Miglia
properties.why_famous: The first Brescia–Rome–Brescia race established Italy's thousand-mile public-road classic.
properties.route_summary: 1927 anticlockwise circuit via Parma, Bologna, Florence, Siena and Rome, returning via Umbria, the Adriatic, Treviso and Verona.
properties.source_title: 1000 Miglia: The first race in 1927
properties.geometry_note: Edition-specific town sequence differs substantially from 1955 and modern revival routes; straight links are not historical road centerlines.
properties.description: Edition-specific town sequence differs substantially from 1955 and modern revival routes; straight links are not historical road centerlines.

properties.title: First Monaco Grand Prix
properties.why_famous: The first Monaco Grand Prix turned the principality's city streets into a motor-racing icon.
properties.route_summary: One 1929 Boulevard Albert I–Casino–Station–Portier–harbour–Gasometer loop, repeated 100 times.
properties.source_title: Automobile Club de Monaco: Club history
properties.geometry_note: Historic corner sequence with approximate coordinates. The 1929 Station Hairpin, tunnel and Gasometer differ from later roadworks and today's circuit.
properties.description: Historic corner sequence with approximate coordinates. The 1929 Station Hairpin, tunnel and Gasometer differ from later roadworks and today's circuit.
properties.overview: The first Monaco Grand Prix turned the principality's city streets into a motor-racing icon.

properties.source_title: Automobile Club de l'Ouest: Le Mans 66 archive

properties.description: 1966 period circuit schematic, avoiding post-1990 Mulsanne chicanes and later infield sections. One loop shown; race mileage depends on laps.

properties.title: First U.S. Army transcontinental motor convoy
properties.why_famous: The Army's first coast-to-coast motor convoy tested whether heavy military vehicles could cross the United States; Dwight Eisenhower's experience later informed his support for improved national highways.
properties.route_summary: Washington's Zero Milestone to Gettysburg, then the 1919 Lincoln Highway corridor through the Midwest, Wyoming, Utah and Nevada to Oakland; the convoy ferried across San Francisco Bay to its terminus.
properties.source_title: Eisenhower Presidential Library — 1919 convoy daily log
properties.geometry_note: Named towns and the final Oakland–San Francisco ferry come from the Army's day-by-day log. The line between them is a corridor, not a digitization of 1919 roadbeds; the convoy made local detours and the Lincoln Highway alignment changed over time.

additional_sources.title: Eisenhower Library expedition summary
additional_sources.note: Confirms dates, 3,251-mile scope and Eisenhower's participation.

properties.title: 1903 Gordon Bennett Cup — Irish road circuit
properties.why_famous: This international automobile race made the closed public-road circuit a model for early Grand Prix racing; Camille Jenatzy won for Germany in a Mercedes.
properties.route_summary: The figure-eight Athy circuit combined an eastern loop through Castledermot and Carlow with a western loop through Kildare, Monasterevin, the Heath and Stradbally.
properties.source_title: Into Kildare — historic Gordon Bennett route brochure
properties.geometry_note: The two documented loops are drawn once each; the 1903 race repeated them (three eastern and four western laps). Town and control coordinates approximate the historic road course, not present-day driving directions. Ballyshannon is the Kildare crossroads, not the Donegal town.

additional_sources.title: Contemporary course map reproduced by motoring historians
additional_sources.note: Period route map shows the figure-eight control sequence.
